active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.dual_annealing on a gauge-fixed, exact nonsmooth ratio objective to search for a genuinely asymmetric basin
active_paradigms.description: The current program first uses a large batched soft-extrema flow and then SLSQP polishing. Its strength is that it starts from the relevant antipodal seven-line seed and eventually optimizes the actual epigraph constraints; this explains why it reaches the reference score. Its weakness is that the high-power softmax stages and the final SLSQP call are strongly local, so they mostly preserve the seed’s contact topology and can miss a slightly better asymmetric diameter/contact graph. Replace the population continuation and SLSQP polish by one direct global call to scipy.optimize.dual_annealing on a 36-dimensional gauge-fixed coordinate vector: fix point 0 at the origin, point 1 on the x-axis, and point 2 in the xy-plane. The scalar objective should be negative min(d2)/max(d2), evaluated directly from all 91 squared distances, with a large finite penalty for coincident points or numerically degenerate gauges. Use broad but finite coordinate bounds, such as [-1,1] for free coordinates, because scale is removed inside the objective by dividing by dmax. Seed x0 from the existing seven-direction construction, but let annealing use reannealing and local search to alter contact combinatorics rather than merely perturbing a known basin. Return the best normalized geometry seen by the objective, not the annealer’s nominal termination point. This is fundamentally different from the failed differential-evolution attempt because it searches the full gauge-fixed 14-point geometry rather than an antipodal seven-direction angular family.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The exact evaluator quantity min_pair_squared_distance / max_pair_squared_distance; prioritize discovering a contact graph different from the current near-antipodal local basin.
active_paradigms.cautions: The raw objective is nonsmooth whenever the identity of a closest or farthest pair changes, so do not use a soft surrogate in the reported selection criterion. Keep a deterministic seed and a strict iteration/time budget. Gauge fixing must not accidentally force an incorrect orientation; choose a noncollinear third point from the seed and parameterize only its x and y entries. Since the known score is already within roughly 1.6e-5 of reference, only accept a candidate after recomputing all pairwise distances in float64 and normalizing by its actual diameter.

active_paradigms.idea: Derive an exact low-dimensional contact-family parameterization from the observed active graph and solve it with sympy.nsolve
active_paradigms.description: The present code already exposes the valuable clue that the solution is extremely close to a structured 14-point configuration, but its SLSQP epigraph formulation treats all 39 geometric degrees of freedom independently. Inspect the returned best configuration offline and classify edges into diameter edges, shortest-contact edges, and clearly slack edges with a tolerance around 1e-6. Use graph automorphisms of this active graph to partition vertices into symmetry orbits, then parameterize one representative coordinate per orbit and generate the full 14-point set through the inferred rotations/reflections or paired affine relations. Impose equations saying every shortest-contact edge has squared length t, every diameter edge has squared length 1, plus centroid and gauge equations; the unknowns are orbit parameters and t. Call sympy.nsolve once at high precision, for example 80 to 150 decimal digits, starting from the numerical configuration. This turns the nearly singular nonsmooth constrained optimization into solving a small equal-distance algebraic system, potentially recovering the exact reference geometry rather than a floating-point approximate stationary point. After converting the high-precision coordinates back to float64, test every non-contact edge; if all are strictly between t and 1, the solution is a valid candidate and often improves the score simply by eliminating the 1e-5-scale residual imbalance left by soft descent and SLSQP.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Numerical precision and exact equality of the true shortest and diameter contact classes, thereby reducing residual spread that lowers the squared ratio.
active_paradigms.cautions: This should be based on an empirically verified active graph, not an assumed antipodal symmetry: the failed KKT root approach likely failed because it solved an overdetermined or incorrectly guessed active set. Include only independent equal-distance equations, and reject the solve if any nominally slack pair violates [t,1] after normalization. High-precision symbolic/numerical solving can be slow, so keep the orbit-reduced system small and use fixed initial values derived from the deterministic seed.

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.optimize.milp to select a promising diameter/contact graph before reconstructing its geometry analytically
active_paradigms.description: The key limitation of the current continuous method is contact-topology blindness: it only discovers which pairs are active after moving coordinates. Instead, use a discrete graph screen to identify plausible optimal combinatorial skeletons. Construct binary variables for candidate shortest edges and candidate diameter edges on the 14 vertices, enforce degree patterns observed in the current solution or in nearby perturbations, require enough shortest contacts for rigidity, forbid an edge from belonging to both classes, and impose symmetry-breaking labels. Add linear incidence constraints ensuring the candidate graph is connected and that diameter edges can support the required width structure; maximize a rigidity/contact-quality surrogate such as total weighted contact degree while penalizing highly uneven vertex degrees. Use scipy.optimize.milp once to obtain the best graph under these combinatorial conditions. For each selected graph family, use its automorphism/orbit structure to write a deterministic coordinate ansatz with equal shortest and diameter lengths, rather than running another generic continuous optimizer. The value is not that MILP evaluates distances itself, but that it can force exploration of contact graphs excluded by the current antipodal initialization and can identify a smaller algebraic family suitable for exact reconstruction. This separates the discrete choice of active pairs from the continuous realization, which is precisely where softmax force descent is weakest.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Exploration of alternative rigid contact and diameter graphs that could have a larger exact min/max squared-distance ratio than the current locally selected graph.
active_paradigms.cautions: MILP alone cannot certify Euclidean realizability or optimize the ratio, so its output must be treated only as a graph hypothesis and checked by a deterministic geometric construction. Do not encode arbitrary quadratic distance constraints as linear constraints. Calibrate allowed degrees from actual near-best configurations, otherwise graph constraints may eliminate the true topology. Keep the candidate edge set sparse, for example pairs that become near-active across deterministic perturbations, to avoid a large and uninformative binary model.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace soft-extrema force descent with a direct antipodal line-packing SLSQP formulation
tried_paradigms.description: The current program is a large batched continuation method: it starts mainly from seven antipodal directions, optimizes a soft minimum-minus-maximum log-distance objective, and sharpens the soft extrema through powers up to 1920. Its strength is broad deterministic basin coverage and stable scale/translation removal, which is why it nearly reaches the reference. Its limiting weakness is that the final objective remains a noisy subgradient approximation to a nonsmooth max/min problem, so it oscillates between changing active pairs rather than satisfying the active inequalities exactly. Exploit the apparent antipodal structure explicitly by optimizing seven unit vectors v_i and returning [v_1,...,v_7,-v_1,...,-v_7]. Introduce a scalar mu and call scipy.optimize.minimize once with method='SLSQP', objective mu, equality constraints ||v_i||^2=1, and inequalities mu-dot(v_i,v_j)>=0 and mu+dot(v_i,v_j)>=0 for every i<j. For an antipodal set the diameter is exactly 2 and the squared evaluator ratio is exactly (1-mu)/2, so this constrained problem directly optimizes the evaluator rather than a surrogate. Remove rotational null directions by fixing one direction to the z axis and one coordinate of a second direction, and use a fixed high-quality seven-line seed encoded in the program.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly minimize maximum absolute inner product mu; this maximizes the evaluator's squared ratio (1-mu)/2 for the antipodal construction and should remove the remaining roughly 0.1% soft-objective gap.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Use analytic constraint Jacobians if possible and tight ftol/maxiter because the target improvement is very small. Verify all seven norms and all 21 absolute inner products after the call, then construct exact negatives so that dmax is reliably 2. A generic random initialization is unlikely to reach the correct contact graph; use one deterministic near-optimal seed, not repeated optimization calls.

tried_paradigms.idea: Solve the active contact graph's KKT equations to obtain a high-precision stationary spherical code
tried_paradigms.description: Treat the near-reference configuration as a seven-line packing problem rather than as 14 unconstrained particles. From a fixed close antipodal seed, determine offline which signed inner-product constraints attain the largest absolute value and hard-code that signed contact graph in the submitted program. Build a square KKT residual system containing unit-norm equations, equality equations s_ij dot(v_i,v_j)-mu=0 for the selected contacts, and tangential force-balance equations using one multiplier per contact. Call scipy.optimize.root once, preferably with method='lm' for an overdetermined residual formulation or method='hybr' after removing rotational gauge freedoms. The resulting root enforces equal active contacts and stationarity simultaneously, which is exactly what the current decaying soft-force iterations only approximate. Evaluate the actual maximum absolute dot product of the returned vectors, not merely the nominal mu, and return the corresponding seven vectors and their negatives.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Numerical polishing of the active constraints and force balance, aiming to turn a nearly optimal soft-minimum solution into an accurately realized local optimum with a smaller true maximum coherence.
tried_paradigms.cautions: This only works when the hard-coded contact graph and signs match the intended optimum; an incorrect graph may converge to a saddle or an infeasible code. Eliminate the three rotational degrees of freedom before making the system square, and reject roots with negative or implausibly large contact multipliers if the KKT convention requires nonnegative multipliers. The fixed approximate seed and graph should be obtained during development and embedded; do not run the current long continuation followed by root solving at evaluation time.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use differential evolution on a compact seven-direction angular parameterization to test globally different line-packing basins
tried_paradigms.description: The current population includes asymmetric 14-point starts, but its gradient flow is strongly attracted to the original antipodal/cubic-tetrahedral basin and may never discover a distinct contact graph. Parameterize seven unoriented unit directions by spherical angles, fixing the first direction and a rotational gauge so that only about eleven to fourteen bounded variables remain. Define the direct objective as max_{i<j}|dot(v_i,v_j)|; after optimization return the seven directions and their negatives. Invoke scipy.optimize.differential_evolution once with a fixed seed, a moderate population, deferred updating, workers=1 for reproducibility, and polish=False, so the single global call searches contact-graph topology rather than following the current soft-extrema trajectory. This objective is compact, bounded, and is exactly equivalent to the evaluator ratio within the antipodal family. Include a deterministic near-reference angular vector in the initial population if supported, while reserving the rest of that one population for broad exploration.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Global improvement of maximum coherence across qualitatively different seven-line contact graphs; it can either find a genuinely better code or establish a better seed for a later independently developed exact construction.
tried_paradigms.cautions: Raw 42-coordinate differential evolution is prohibitively expensive and has redundant translation/scale/rotation modes; the reduced spherical-angle representation is essential. The max-absolute-dot objective is nonsmooth, so do not rely on the default local polishing stage. Bound runtime via maxiter and popsize, and always normalize reconstructed directions before returning them to avoid angular roundoff changing the diameter ratio.

tried_paradigms.idea: Replace the soft-extrema continuation with one direct constrained SLSQP solve of the epigraph formulation.
tried_paradigms.description: The current program is a large batched projected-gradient search: it starts from an antipodal 7-direction code and random spherical starts, then maximizes a smooth approximation of log(dmin/dmax) while progressively increasing the soft-min/soft-max power. Its strengths are scale/translation removal, many concurrent basins, and a final near-active-set phase, which explains why it is already within about 0.1% of the reference. Its limiting weakness is that soft extrema still bias the solution toward non-active pairs and normalized fixed steps cannot enforce the true distance inequalities exactly. Parameterize 13 points after fixing one point at the origin, fix a second point on the x-axis and a third in the xy-plane to remove rigid motions, and include a scalar t. Use scipy.optimize.minimize(method="SLSQP") once on the best current configuration, maximizing t subject to every squared distance being at least t and at most 1, with the current diameter pair scaled to one initially. Supply exact analytic Jacobians for all 91 lower and upper distance constraints, tight ftol, and a generous maxiter, because this is the evaluator’s stated epigraph problem rather than a surrogate. Return the coordinate portion of the feasible solution after optionally rescaling by its measured maximum distance.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly maximize t=(dmin/dmax)^2, exactly the evaluator’s min_max_ratio and therefore combined_score; feasibility of the active shortest-pair and diameter constraints is the priority.
tried_paradigms.cautions: SLSQP is local and the formulation is nonconvex, so initialize from the current best antipodal-search result rather than a generic random array. Do not constrain a diameter pair to equal one by assumption unless it is also represented by the all-pairs upper constraints; the actual identity of the diameter can switch. Carefully remove only rigid-motion degrees of freedom, not shape degrees of freedom, and provide finite coordinates even if SLSQP reports a mild line-search warning.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use deterministic differential evolution on a gauge-fixed exact ratio objective to search asymmetric basins that the antipodal seed population may miss.
tried_paradigms.description: The existing method strongly favors antipodal configurations because half of its population is generated as perturbations of an explicitly antipodal base, and even its spherical starts are quickly attracted by the same soft-force landscape. This is efficient for finding a nearly optimal spherical-code-like arrangement, but it can miss a slightly asymmetric configuration with a better exact extreme-distance ratio. Construct a reduced 33-dimensional coordinate parameterization by fixing translation and orientation, and evaluate the exact objective min(pairwise squared distances)/max(pairwise squared distances) directly, not a power-mean surrogate. Call scipy.optimize.differential_evolution once with a fixed seed, Sobol initialization, mutation dithering, workers=1 for reproducibility, and bounds wide enough to contain normalized configurations. Add a deterministic normalization inside the objective by centering and dividing by RMS radius before computing the ratio, so coordinate magnitude does not consume search range. Set polish=True only if its internal final local operation is acceptable in the runtime environment; otherwise rely on a sufficiently large population and iterations. This supplies genuinely global, nonsymmetric exploration rather than another temperature schedule around the same seeds.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Escape the current projected soft-extrema basin and maximize the exact squared pairwise ratio, particularly by testing whether the true 14-point optimum breaks the imposed antipodal structure.
tried_paradigms.cautions: The raw min/max objective is nonsmooth and differential evolution in 33 dimensions can be expensive, so use a realistic population/iteration budget and retain the best known configuration as one member of the initialization population if supported. Gauge fixing must not accidentally force a particular pair to be the diameter. Avoid parallel workers because evaluator import/runtime behavior and reproducibility can become unreliable.

tried_paradigms.idea: Perform an active-contact rigidity polish by solving equal-distance contact equations with a single scipy root solve.
tried_paradigms.description: Near the current score, only a small set of shortest pairs and longest pairs determines the evaluator, whereas the current high-power gradients continue to receive weak contributions from many inactive pairs. First inspect the current returned configuration deterministically and form two contact graphs using pairs within a very small relative tolerance of dmin and dmax. Fix translation, rotation, and scale with coordinate gauges, then use scipy.optimize.root once on equations that set all selected short contacts to a common squared length, all selected diameter contacts to one, and impose stationarity through contact-force equilibrium weights or a minimally determined independent subset of those equations. The goal is to move from a soft-objective stationary point to a rigid realization of the actual active contact pattern. After root convergence, verify all 91 distances and retain the root result only if its exact evaluator ratio exceeds the unpolished configuration. If the contact pattern is overdetermined, select equations using a rank-revealing QR of their numerical Jacobian so the root system is square and non-singular. This approach is qualitatively different from global search: it treats the nearly optimal geometry as a contact-framework realization problem and can recover the final missing digits once the correct graph has been found.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: The exact gap between the active shortest-distance shell and active diameter shell; eliminate residual inequality slack or imbalance left by soft-max continuation.
tried_paradigms.cautions: A root solver does not itself enforce all inactive inequalities, so always evaluate every pair after solving and reject any candidate that creates a newly shorter pair or longer diameter. Contact-set thresholds should be relative to the measured distances and conservative enough not to include clearly inactive pairs. The gauge and equation count must be consistent; otherwise singularity is expected and the original configuration should be returned.
